rationale: The PI3K/Akt and Ras/MAPK/ERK pathways cross-regulate extensively in breast epithelium. Akt supports ERK activation through Raf and through mTORC1-dependent translation, so inhibiting Akt lowers pERK1/2. Conversely, MEK inhibition relieves ERK-dependent negative feedback on receptor tyrosine kinases and IRS/GAB adaptors, and the textbook consequence is a rebound rise in pAkt T308. Each inhibitor of course lowers its own readout: pAkt T308 falls under the Akt inhibitor and pERK1/2 falls under UO126, which is the expected on-target effect of acting at each node.
